parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A solenoid of diameter 6.0 cm and 540 turns is placed in a uniform magnetic field as shown in Fig. 9.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The variation with time *t* of the magnetic flux density is shown in Fig. 9.2.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate the maximum magnitude of the induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) in the solenoid.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
A thin copper sheet X is supported on a rigid rod so that it hangs between the poles of a magnet as shown in Fig. 9.3.

[[fig:f3]]

Sheet X is displaced to one side and then released so that it oscillates. A motion sensor is used to record the displacement of X.

A second thin copper sheet Y replaces sheet X. Sheet Y has the same overall dimensions as X but is cut into the shape shown in Fig. 9.4.

[[fig:f4]]

The motion sensor is again used to record the displacement.

The graph in Fig. 9.5 shows the variation with time *t* of the displacement *s* of each copper sheet.

[[fig:f5]]
parts.text: State the name of the phenomenon illustrated by the gradual reduction in the amplitude of the dashed line.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce which copper sheet is represented by the dashed line. Explain your answer using the principles of electromagnetic induction.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.1
figures.alt: A solenoid is shown in a magnetic field, with a diameter of 6.0 cm and a label indicating 540 turns.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.2
figures.alt: A graph of magnetic flux density in mT against time in seconds rises linearly from zero to 250 mT, stays constant, then falls linearly to zero.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.3
figures.alt: A copper sheet X hanging from a rod is shown between the poles of a magnet.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.4
figures.alt: Copper sheet Y is shown with a circular hole near the top and several long vertical slots cut into its lower section.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.5
figures.alt: A displacement-time graph shows solid and dashed oscillating curves, with the dashed curve decreasing in amplitude.
